title: gmat R integration
text:
Serializable objects

gsuite_bed_resource retains canonical BED/BIM/FAM paths, physical counts, and literal ordered BIM/FAM metadata.
gsuite_bed_panel retains component resources, exact selections, selected metadata, and zero-based native source mappings.
gsuite_sparse_ld retains the output prefix and five resource paths, dimensions, settings, execution mode, and disk marker sidecar. The CSR payload stays on disk.

These list-style S3 objects have no external pointers. Later operations reopen and validate paths; gsuite_sparse_ld_open() reconstructs a descriptor from a prefix in a fresh session.

title: gmat R integration
text:
Identity and ordering
Component order is list order. Components must have identical ordered (family_id, individual_id) pairs before selection. Sample identities and per-component marker IDs are resolved exactly, and requested order is preserved. Global marker order concatenates component selections. Duplicate or missing identities are errors. Nothing silently sorts chromosomes, positions, markers, samples, or alleles.
Annotation tables require explicit unique marker row names and unique column names. Their marker-ID set must equal the disk marker set; rows may be supplied in another order because gmat realigns them by exact identity. Column order is preserved.

title: gmat R integration
text:
Numerical contract
Raw PLINK dosage counts BIM allele 1 (00 → 2, 01 → missing, 10 → 1, 11 → 0). Sparse LD centres and scales observed dosage using \(p=\operatorname{mean}(g)/2\) and \(\sqrt{2p(1-p)}\); missing calls become standardized zero. Only same-chromosome pairs inside every active distance window are considered, and \(r^2\geq\texttt{r2\_threshold}\) is retained. The disk CSR stores sorted strict-upper float correlations and has an implicit unit diagonal.
Ordinary, finite-sample-corrected, partitioned, and corrected partitioned scores stream the validated disk CSR. Corrected off-diagonal contributions are \(r^2-\frac{1-r^2}{N-2}\) with N from disk metadata and are not clamped. Annotation values may be binary, overlapping, continuous, negative, or zero.
Window boundaries are inclusive and positive windows are combined. Disabling both requires explicit full-LD authorization. Disk creation validates a same- directory staging set before publication, refuses existing owned targets by default, and publishes metadata last. The gs_gprep(task = "sparseld") contract and compatibility views are specified in sparse-LD preparation.

title: gmat R integration
text:
Limitations
The binding does not harmonize alleles, flip dosage, convert genome builds, parse summary statistics, fit LD-score regressions, create dense LD, or add a general matrix class. All five files in a persistent gmat resource must remain available together.
See the gmat method catalogue for the complete native contracts.

title: Marker-QC contract
text:
gs_gfilter() is gsuite’s summary-only marker-selection operation. It accepts the strict serializable c("gs_genotypes", "Glist") descriptor produced by gs_gprep(task = "prepare") and returns a plain marker-ID vector. It does not mutate the descriptor, read packed BED genotype bytes, write BED or CSR files, decode a genotype matrix, or construct sparse LD. gmat and gbits remain unchanged owners of metadata/LD and packed-genotype operations respectively.
Marker identity is canonical chromosome/file/BIM order. Every required chromosome-wise field is checked for the same shape, and IDs must be complete and globally unique. The existing preparation validator also reopens the BIM/FAM/BED descriptors and verifies source mappings. Genotype counts must be nonnegative integers whose sum equals the exact summary population recorded by sample_source_indices_0based and provenance$summary_samples. MAF must agree with n0, n1, and n2. Thus a study-sample preparation uses that selected population rather than the complete FAM count.



Each enabled rule creates a full-length exclusion mask; the final mask is their union. NULL disables a numeric rule and FALSE disables a logical rule.

MAF excludes \(\mathrm{maf}_j\leq\texttt{maf}\); equality is excluded.
Missingness is \(\frac{n_{\mathrm{miss}}}{n_0+n_1+n_2+n_{\mathrm{miss}}}\) and excludes values strictly greater than missing; equality is retained.
HWE excludes exact-test p-values strictly less than hwe; equality is retained.
INFO excludes values strictly less than info; equality is retained.
Ambiguity excludes the exact allele pairs A/T, T/A, C/G, and G/C.
The indel/non-SNP rule retains only exact uppercase single-base A, C, G, or T for both alleles. It therefore rejects multi-base, symbolic, and lowercase encodings without silently normalizing alleles.
MHC excludes a closed interval, including both endpoints, on stored chromosome labels 6 and chr6: GRCh37 [28,477,797, 33,448,397], or GRCh38 [28,510,120, 33,480,577]. The assembly must be explicitly GRCh37 or GRCh38, supplied as an argument or in Glist$assembly; it is never guessed.

All numeric thresholds are finite scalars in [0,1]. Logical controls are nonmissing scalars. A marker-aligned INFO field is required only when INFO filtering is enabled. It may be a named numeric vector or list, but its names must be a duplicate-free exact set of prepared marker IDs. Values are reordered by identity into canonical order before the mask is calculated.



For each biallelic marker, gsuite conditions on the observed sample count and minor-allele copy count and enumerates every feasible heterozygote count with the same allele total. The two-sided p-value is the sum of conditional genotype probabilities no greater than the observed genotype probability. Probabilities within relative tolerance 1e-12 are treated as ties. This is the conventional probability-ordering exact test. Monomorphic markers receive p-value 1. All-missing or structurally invalid counts are descriptor errors; any otherwise nonfinite HWE result is conservatively excluded when HWE filtering is enabled.
qgg 1.1.6 instead uses a one-degree-of-freedom Pearson chi-square calculation. The tested version’s gfilter() also has disabled-mask hazards, relies on incomplete positional/name alignment, and subsets its combined mask incorrectly during INFO filtering. gsuite deliberately uses the exact test, complete identity validation, independent full-length masks, and an explicit default HWE threshold of 1e-12. It also freezes the documented inclusive MAF boundary.



Glist <- gs_gprep(
  study = "Reference",
  bedfiles = bedfiles,
  task = "prepare",
  nthreads = 4
)

rsids <- gs_gfilter(
  Glist,
  maf = 0.01,
  missing = 0.05,
  hwe = 1e-12,
  ambiguous = TRUE,
  indels = TRUE
)

Glist <- gs_gprep(
  Glist = Glist,
  task = "sparseld",
  rsids = rsids,
  out_prefix = "reference_ld",
  nthreads = 4
)
Preparation computes reusable summaries once. The same unchanged descriptor can be filtered under several policies, and sparse LD is subsequently built only for the selected markers.

title: Architecture
text:
gsuite is the unified interface to a modular family of independently versioned computational libraries. Each native library owns a narrow data, numerical, or statistical boundary and remains independently buildable. The current gsuite R package exposes the public combinations recorded in the authoritative model catalog; it is not necessarily a binding for every native entry point.
gsuite and gsim are the user-facing R packages. gsim generates genotype, pedigree and observation data; gsuite provides analysis interfaces. The tutorial connects them through ordinary R data frames.

text:
Responsibilities



Library
Responsibility
Immediate boundary




gbits
Packed genotype storage, PLINK BED access, selections, transformations, genotype products, and weighted covariance/normal operators
Does not own genomic resource metadata, general solvers, or statistical models


gmat
BED/BIM/FAM resources, ordered panels, sparse-LD construction and storage, sparse-LD algebra, and LD scores
Delegates BED decoding to gbits and does not fit LD-score regressions


gsolve
Model-independent dense, sparse, and matrix-free operators, factorizations, preconditioned conjugate gradient, probes, and stochastic log determinants
Contains no genotype, likelihood, or mixed-model semantics


greml
ML/REML covariance models, exact and stochastic inference, sparse mixed-model equations, optimization, prediction, and uncertainty
Uses gsolve for numerical primitives and does not own genotype formats


gcorr
Ordinary and partitioned single-trait LDSC, cross-trait and multivariate LDSC, genetic covariance/correlation, enrichment, jackknife uncertainty, and diagnostics
Consumes gmat LD scores and does not construct or store LD


gscore
Standalone specialized high-performance multi-score application directly from PLINK BED
Owns the scoring kernel, not metadata preparation, allele alignment, or general matrix operators


gsim
User-facing R simulation of genotypes, pedigrees and observation records
Owns simulation workflows; generated data can be used in gsuite analyses


gbayes
Future Bayesian inference library
Planned; no implemented dependency or method contract exists yet


gsuite
Unified R/native entry point and suite-level integration documentation
Currently binds selected gsolve, greml, gbits and gmat capabilities and requires the gbits gsolve adapter




How the R interface connects the components
The pedigree data-frame workflow normalizes short covariance specifications and explicit gvc() components into one internal model description. Formulas define fixed and random bases, variables bind record IDs, kernels define relationships, covariance descriptors declare coordinates and optional starts, and the task selects REML or a fixed solve. The adapter owns R validation, sparse fixed-design construction and result labels; it calls the existing specialized pedigree interfaces or the public component-LMM constructors and fitters for independent groups of random intercepts. A named vector of grouping columns in one gvc() declares correlated channels sharing a pedigree or identity relationship; separate descriptors remain independent. Residual group, structure, block and time fields bind data columns to existing grouped, AR(1) and exponential component residual constructors. Missing-response filtering is shared by phenotypes, incidence and residual metadata. No new native numerical implementation or dense relationship matrix is introduced. formula and formulas are equivalent; supplied starts do not select a different route. An explicit gs_fit_control() object selects the specialized compiled interface. General sparse-direct defaults use CHOLMOD selected inversion; independent components reuse gs_lmm_control().

Owner

This graph describes current build dependencies. Each arrow points from a dependent component to a library it requires. Its independent build does not change its role as the ecosystem’s scoring library. gsim is a separate user-facing R package; its simulation-to-analysis workflow exchanges data with gsuite and is not a native-library dependency. The planned gbayes library is intentionally absent from the graph until it has an implemented public dependency contract.

title: Architecture
text:
Ownership rules

File-format decoding and packed genotype algebra belong to gbits; reusable genomic resource identity, sparse LD, and LD scores belong to gmat.
Numerical operators and solvers belong to gsolve; ML/REML model semantics and inference belong to greml.
LD-score regression and its uncertainty belong to gcorr, not gmat.
Direct multi-score BED application belongs to gscore. Its standalone design is the current implementation boundary.
The gsuite package translates explicit R values into existing public native contracts; it does not reimplement their algorithms.
New cross-library dependencies require a demonstrated contract and must follow the existing direction without introducing cycles.

text:
1. Start with the question and data
You might ask:

I have body-weight records, sex, cohort and herd, plus a pedigree. Help me estimate additive genetic variation and predict animal effects. First inspect the data and explain any issues that affect the analysis.

The assistant checks the column meanings and measurement units with you, then inspects missing values, duplicated records, factor levels and phenotype distributions. It checks that observation IDs match the pedigree, parent IDs are represented consistently, and pedigree relationships are valid. Repeated measurements require particular attention: several records per animal may need a different model from one observation per animal.
For a reproducible demonstration, use the Prepare ordinary data frames section and the data preparation at the start of Single trait in the pedigree tutorial. That supplies pedigree and data, including BW, sex, cohort, herd and id. For your study, use your own data frames instead.
str(data)
summary(data)
colSums(is.na(data))
anyDuplicated(pedigree$id)
setdiff(data$id, pedigree$id)
table(table(data$id))
These are initial checks, not a complete data-validation procedure. The assistant records issues and proposed changes in a data-check summary. Decisions such as excluding records or recoding missing parents belong in the analysis script, with an explanation you can review.

2. Translate the question into a model
You might ask:

Treat sex, cohort and herd as fixed effects. Use the pedigree for additive genetic animal effects. Explain the assumptions and show me the model code.

For the tutorial’s single-trait model:
\[
y = X\beta + Za + e,\qquad
\operatorname{Var}(a)=\sigma_a^2 A,\qquad
\operatorname{Var}(e)=\sigma_e^2 I.
\]
Here \(A\) is the pedigree relationship matrix. The model assumes independent animal and residual effects and a common residual variance. Whether herd should be fixed, and whether additional environmental effects are needed, depends on the study design and your scientific question.

fit_diagnostics$converged

title: Formula and variance-component compiled-MME REML
text:
For the new data-frame shorthand, optional starts, fixed solves and genetic random regression, begin with Pedigree analysis. Both formula and formulas now use the same general adapter. This page documents the specialized compiled-MME route, explicitly requested with a gs_fit_control() object, complete explicit covariance starts, and task = "reml". Its result layout remains specialized. Supplying starts alone does not select it. General fits accept named controls for the selected pedigree or component fitter. Compiled controls now default to CHOLMOD selected inversion.
The data-frame gs_pedigree() constructor described here is distinct from gs_model_pedigree(), the ordered-parent constructor used by the persistent-model API. The two signatures are not interchangeable and do not dispatch implicitly.
gfit() is gsuite’s direct formula REML entry point. Model incidence comes from formulas, pedigree relationships come from gs_pedigree(), and explicit positive-interior covariance starts come from named gvc() components. The interface lowers one immutable model to greml’s public compiled-MME plan, creates one numerical session, optimizes, and finalizes BLUPs from the retained accepted response state.
PED <- gs_pedigree(pedigree, id = "id", sire = "sire", dam = "dam")

fit <- gfit(
  BW ~ sex + batch + (1 | id),
  records,
  list(
    animal = gvc("id", "BW", PED, start = 1),
    residual = gvc("residual", "BW", start = 1)
  ),
  control = gs_fit_control(direct_backend = "cholmod")
)
For multiple traits, formulas is a named list and each component start is an SPD matrix in the declared trait order. Each trait has a separate fixed-effect block. Scalar records are ordered by formula-list order and original data-row order. An NA response is absent; observed traits from the same data row form one complete or incomplete patterned residual unit. Missing fixed covariates, nonfinite observed responses, and missing pedigree identifiers are errors.


From the repository root, with gsuite installed, run:
source("tools/examples/run_single_trait_pedigree_example.R")
The complete example starts with two ordinary data frames: data has one observation per row (id, BW, factor sex, continuous covariate x); pedigree has one animal per row (id, sire, dam). It reuses the small deterministic BW formula-test illustration, not a random draw from the fitted pedigree model. Its artificial sex labels vary across records of an animal; real data should use consistent animal sex. These toy values illustrate the API, not biological inference or variance recovery.
The formula BW ~ sex + x + (1 | id) supplies fixed effects and animal incidence. A separate gs_pedigree() relationship and named animal and residual components supply covariance structure and positive starting variances. Under this model, animal covariance is the pedigree relationship times the animal variance; residuals are independent with a common variance. Repeated observations share the animal effect, with no additional permanent environment effect. Starts are not fixed variances.
IDs, not row positions, align the tables. Pedigree rows may be reordered; unknown parents use NA, while known parents must be listed. Observation IDs absent from the pedigree are errors. Animal a8 has no observations but remains in the pedigree and receives a conditional animal prediction from relatives.
summary(fit) displays covariance estimates and convergence, coef(fit) returns fixed effects, and the public fit$random_effects$animal table contains IDs and animal BLUPs (not full predicted body weights). fit$converged and fit$convergence_reason expose the stopping result. Prediction tables follow pedigree order, so compare them by ID. Prediction for new data and prediction uncertainty are not supported on this formula route.
For development verification only, select the existing isolated installation before sourcing the same example:

source("tools/examples/run_single_trait_pedigree_example.R")



The only random grammar is exactly (1 | variable). A scalar formula has one or two distinct terms, with at most one pedigree component and one independent identity component. Multitrait formulas retain one shared pedigree term. Random slopes, more than two terms, duplicate terms, ||, nesting, crossing, functions, interactions, and expressions on the grouping side are rejected. After removing the random terms, base R model.frame() and model.matrix() build the fixed design and preserve coefficient names, contrasts, factor levels, and the formula environment.
Random incidence is never materialized as an R matrix. Each observed scalar record supplies a pedigree entity ID, trait/member ID, residual unit and coordinate, and a unit random-intercept weight directly to the compiled-MME specification. This first version may materialize a dense R fixed-effect model.matrix() and therefore targets moderate in-memory data frames.



Scalar fits accept one identity component, one pedigree component, or one of each, plus one homogeneous residual component. Formula order determines the random coefficient blocks and covariance-parameter order. Pedigree levels use external pedigree order, including unphenotyped animals. Identity levels use the sorted observed character or integer domain. Every record contributes a unit weight directly to each present component, including the data-induced pedigree/identity cross block; no R incidence matrix is built.
For example, repeatability and a common-environment model use the same bounded composition rule:
ID <- gs_identity()
repeatability <- gfit(
  y ~ sex + (1 | animal_id) + (1 | permanent_id), records,
  list(
    animal = gvc("animal_id", "y", PED, start = 0.8),
    permanent = gvc("permanent_id", "y", ID, start = 0.4),
    residual = gvc("residual", "y", start = 0.3)
  ),
  control = gs_fit_control(direct_backend = "cholmod")
)

common_environment <- gfit(
  y ~ sex + (1 | animal_id) + (1 | environment), records,
  list(
    animal = gvc("animal_id", "y", PED, start = 0.8),
    environment = gvc("environment", "y", ID, start = 0.4),
    residual = gvc("residual", "y", start = 0.3)
  ),
  control = gs_fit_control(direct_backend = "cholmod")
)
Starts remain mandatory finite positive scalars or finite symmetric positive-definite matrices. Covariance boundaries and automatic rank repair are not attempted.
gs_fit_control() maps backend, direct/support threads, exact trace route, optimizer bounds, coefficient dimension, factor memory, selected-inverse workspace, exact trace systems, RHS workspace, and linear-solve controls directly to the public greml session. A failed preflight does not silently change backend, trace route, batch width, or solver. Diagnostics report the required and configured RHS bytes, peak RHS width, resident coefficient vectors, workspace category, limit result, overflow result, and zero numerical work after rejection.
PARDISO uses its own requested internal thread count and coordinate-exact traces. CHOLMOD uses serial support work and selected inversion. Generic support execution remains independent; an unsupported request is returned as not_supported before solver work. No GNU OpenMP layer is introduced.
The returned gs_fit owns covariance estimates, fixed effects, animal BLUPs in external pedigree order, caller-record mappings, optional fitted values, residuals and Py, score/standard-AI diagnostics, optimizer history, resource preflight, work counters, and retained-state diagnostics. print(), summary(), coef(), fitted(), residuals(), logLik(), and nobs() are provided. Record methods fail clearly when record values were omitted.

title: gs_genotypes preparation contract
text:
gs_gprep() implements the bounded "prepare" and "sparseld" tasks. For preparation, gsuite owns argument validation, orchestration, and the returned R descriptor; gmat owns strict BIM/FAM parsing and exact ordered multi-file identity; gbits owns BED header, size, offset, packed-code, and threaded count logic. The existing SNP-major PLINK BED files remain the sole persistent genotype representation. qgg is a read-only behavioural and scientific reference and is not a runtime dependency.
Sparse-LD orchestration is specified separately in sparse-LD preparation. Separate LD-score tasks, genetic-map import, GRMs, association, scoring, and other qgg tasks are not implemented by gs_gprep(). Marker filtering is provided separately by gs_gfilter(). Unknown preparation tasks fail explicitly.



Every BED/BIM/FAM vector is nonempty and has identical length. Omitted companions are derived by replacing only a final case-insensitive .bed suffix. Every path is normalized and must name an existing regular file. gbits requires the exact header 6c 1b 01 and exact size \(3+M\lceil N/4\rceil\); individual-major, truncated, and trailing-byte inputs fail.
The first FAM supplies ids and the complete physical sample order. Individual IDs are nonempty and globally unique. gmat requires every component to have the same exact ordered (family_id, individual_id) sequence; no set-only check or positional permutation is used. With ids = NULL, all samples contribute and study_ids is NULL. A supplied vector is nonempty, unique, nonmissing, fully resolved, retained in caller order, and used only as the summary sample set; ids remains complete.
Every BIM row has six fields, a nonempty chromosome and marker ID, finite nonnegative map position, positive physical position, and distinct nonempty alleles. Source marker IDs are globally unique across every supplied BIM, including unselected rows. BIM order is canonical. A supplied rsids vector is validated completely, then filtered in file/BIM order; caller order is intentionally not retained because the public descriptor remains a file-partitioned physical view. source_marker_indices_0based records every original BIM/BED index, including noncontiguous selections. BED is never rewritten.



a1 is BIM field 5 and a2 BIM field 6. Counts and frequencies always refer to copies of a1:

For \(N_{\mathrm{obs}}=n_0+n_1+n_2\), the returned values are \(\mathrm{af}=\frac{2n_2+n_1}{2N_{\mathrm{obs}}}\), \(\mathrm{af}_1=\mathrm{af}\), \(\mathrm{af}_2=1-\mathrm{af}\), \(\mathrm{maf}=\min(\mathrm{af},1-\mathrm{af})\), \(\mathrm{hom}=(n_0+n_2)/N_{\mathrm{obs}}\), and \(\mathrm{het}=n_1/N_{\mathrm{obs}}\). All-missing selected markers fail with their marker ID. Empirical frequencies are not clipped: monomorphic values are exactly zero or one. This deliberately differs from the tested qgg 1.1.6 reference, whose summaryBED() clips frequencies to [0.00001, 0.99999] and substitutes 0.5 for all-missing markers.



The result is a plain list with class c("gs_genotypes", "Glist"). It carries study, normalized bedfiles/bimfiles/famfiles, complete ids, optional study_ids, n, nchr, m, chromosome/file-wise rsids, mchr, chr, pos, map, a1, a2, cpra, af, af1, af2, maf, nmiss, hom, het, n0, n1, n2, assembly = NULL, physical sample/marker mappings, format and ordering labels, and provenance. It contains neither dense genotypes nor a mandatory external pointer and therefore survives an exact saveRDS()/readRDS() round trip.
The current gsim phenotype workflow can consume ids, rsids, chromosome list structure, and maf. Its default genotype loader remains qgg’s getG, so direct use with this object requires a future small gsuite selected-decode accessor that consumes bedfiles, n, sample_source_indices_0based, and source_marker_indices_0based. That integration is deliberately deferred; no broad qgg compatibility layer is introduced here.



gbits scans packed marker records directly. Selected original offsets are checked with 64-bit arithmetic. Threaded execution assigns deterministic static marker partitions and never calls R from workers. Temporary native storage is \(O(T\lceil N/4\rceil)\) packed bytes for T workers plus \(O(M)\) counts and selection mappings; no \(O(NM)\) decoded matrix exists.

title: Numerical and mixed-model routes
text:
This guide explains route choice and scaling. The model catalog owns capability status, the primitive registry owns reusable mechanism mappings, and architecture owns package dependencies. A native primitive does not establish a qualified public R route.


gsolve owns checked column-major matrix views, leading dimensions, caller-owned workspaces, square and rectangular operators, dense/sparse SPD factors, PCG, preconditioners, deterministic probes, SLQ, and numerical diagnostics. Its operator contracts declare symmetry, definiteness, concurrency, and available diagonals. Rectangular operators provide forward/transpose application and bounded column materialization.
greml owns covariance models, fixed-effect projection, likelihood, score, standard average information (AI), optimization, prediction, and uncertainty. gsuite validates explicit R inputs and translates installed public results. Packed genotype operations belong to gbits; resource identity and LD belong to gmat. The optional gbits adapter supplies numerical operators without a reverse dependency from gsolve or greml to genotype libraries.



For single-trait covariance components, \(V = \sum_c \theta_c K_c\) and
\[
P=V^{-1}-V^{-1}F(F^{\mathsf T}V^{-1}F)^{-1}F^{\mathsf T}V^{-1}.
\]








Route
Computation and storage
Practical boundary




Exact dense
Factors observation covariance V; quadratic storage
Small reference models; prepared genomic BED terms are rejected


Matrix-free covariance
PCG applies inverses/projections; common Hutchinson probes estimate traces and SLQ estimates log determinants
Operator and bounded \(O(nk)\) Krylov/probe storage; solver and stochastic precision must both be adequate


Sparse MME
Assembles coefficient-space statistics and uses a retained sparse factor or a qualified coefficient operator
Fill and resource limits matter; backend, trace, inference, and uncertainty support depend on the specific API


Hybrid covariance
Uses structured sparse terms as a state-matched preconditioner for separately declared matrix-free terms
Components enter once; a pedigree plus genomic sum is not automatic single-step GBLUP


Iterative large-p projection
Nested PCG avoids retaining \(V^{-1}F\) and the full fixed-normal matrix; fixed determinant uses SLQ
Selected contrasts may be available while full fixed-effect covariance is unavailable



The low-level gs_model() sparse/hybrid interface is distinct from the specialized pedigree and component-MME interfaces. In particular, its older limitations must not be applied to all sparse-direct APIs. CHOLMOD selected inversion and PARDISO selected_solve target uncertainty are documented in prediction error. PARDISO selected inversion is unsupported.
Unbalanced multivariate covariance uses the observed principal submatrix of a trait-by-unit covariance: scatter, base-operator application, trait mixing, and gather. Random regression uses supplied basis columns. Neither operation requires a dense production incidence or Kronecker matrix. Selected prediction uncertainty computes only requested target blocks.



Prepared packed BED storage trades preparation work and memory for repeated applications; genomic production routes form no dense GRM. Sparse MME cost depends on coefficient dimension and fill. Matrix-free memory is dominated by operators and bounded Krylov/probe buffers. Nested fixed-effect solves add their own tolerance and determinant-precision requirements.
Independent multiple-RHS PCG solves columns independently. Explicit true block PCG shares a block Krylov recurrence and reports rank compression, deflation, restarts, and each original RHS’s true residual. Its orchestration owns one outer thread. A two-level preconditioner uses a caller-supplied, copied, rank-compressed coarse basis tied to one covariance state; it does not discover a basis automatically. Outer RHS/probe parallelism and operator-local OpenMP must not be nested. Requested and resolved execution are reported separately.
Route selection is API-specific. Low-level model routes are explicit; pedigree direct controls may resolve automatic to an available backend according to their documented policy. An explicit unsupported request does not silently change the statistical route.



The persistent R interface specifies handles, lifetime, ordering, controls, and low-level examples. The formula interface is a separate bounded lowering API. The package qualification limits remain; that page also records the focused constructor naming repair.
Model qualification, qgdata evidence, and the DMU workflow retain scoped numerical evidence and negative outcomes. They do not establish general biobank readiness or universal performance. Build and packaging commands belong in development and binary distribution.

PCG applies inverses/projections; common Hutchinson probes estimate traces and SLQ estimates log determinants
Operator and bounded \(O(nk)\) Krylov/probe storage; solver and stochastic precision must both be adequate

Fill and resource limits matter; backend, trace, inference, and uncertainty support depend on the specific API

Uses structured sparse terms as a state-matched preconditioner for separately declared matrix-free terms
Components enter once; a pedigree plus genomic sum is not automatic single-step GBLUP

In particular, its older limitations must not be applied to all sparse-direct APIs. CHOLMOD selected inversion and PARDISO selected_solve target uncertainty are documented in prediction error. PARDISO selected inversion is unsupported.
Unbalanced multivariate covariance uses the observed principal submatrix of a trait-by-unit covariance: scatter, base-operator application, trait mixing, and gather. Random regression uses supplied basis columns. Neither operation requires a dense production incidence or Kronecker matrix. Selected prediction uncertainty computes only requested target blocks.

title: Numerical and mixed-model routes
text:
Prepared packed BED storage trades preparation work and memory for repeated applications; genomic production routes form no dense GRM. Sparse MME cost depends on coefficient dimension and fill. Matrix-free memory is dominated by operators and bounded Krylov/probe buffers. Nested fixed-effect solves add their own tolerance and determinant-precision requirements.
Independent multiple-RHS PCG solves columns independently. Explicit true block PCG shares a block Krylov recurrence and reports rank compression, deflation, restarts, and each original RHS’s true residual. Its orchestration owns one outer thread. A two-level preconditioner uses a caller-supplied, copied, rank-compressed coarse basis tied to one covariance state; it does not discover a basis automatically. Outer RHS/probe parallelism and operator-local OpenMP must not be nested. Requested and resolved execution are reported separately.
Route selection is API-specific. Low-level model routes are explicit; pedigree direct controls may resolve automatic to an available backend according to their documented policy. An explicit unsupported request does not silently change the statistical route.

title: Numerical and mixed-model routes
text:
The persistent R interface specifies handles, lifetime, ordering, controls, and low-level examples. The formula interface is a separate bounded lowering API. The package qualification limits remain; that page also records the focused constructor naming repair.
Model qualification, qgdata evidence, and the DMU workflow retain scoped numerical evidence and negative outcomes. They do not establish general biobank readiness or universal performance. Build and packaging commands belong in development and binary distribution.

title: Methods
text:
Catalog authority. This page contains route-specific method descriptions and historical version notes. The current suite-wide LMM status is defined by the canonical model catalog, with evidence in model qualification. An exclusion below applies only to the workflow and version being described; it is not a global gsuite capability statement.
This catalogue maps confirmed public capabilities to their owning repository. Implemented means the capability is implemented in development code and exercised by relevant repository validation; it does not claim production-scale qualification. Experimental identifies a present but deliberately provisional integration surface. Planned identifies work with no current public implementation.
The pedigree tutorial adds a bounded R convenience adapter, without adding a statistical model or numerical backend. It covers one pedigree random intercept for one or multiple traits, and single-response genetic random regression with one homogeneous residual. Short and explicit components share normalization; omitted REML starts reuse the existing fixed-effect residual-variance initializers (basis-scaled for random regression). Supplied starts remain authoritative. Fixed solves require all covariances. Multitrait rows identify residual observation units; missing responses are omitted trait by trait. Covariance boundaries, ambiguous kernel assignments and unsupported combinations are not silently repaired. The public examples default to 10,000 simulated animals and do not change broader workload or platform qualification claims.
Explicit scalar gvc() models additionally support multiple independent pedigree and identity random intercepts through the existing component-LMM engine. This includes animal plus permanent environment and animal plus common-group effects. Both formula argument spellings have identical dispatch; starting values do not choose the engine. Omitted scalar starts divide the fixed-design residual variance equally among all random and residual components; supplied starts remain unchanged. All values are required for a fixed solve. Cross-component covariance, multi-component multitrait/random regression and multi-response residual specifications remain outside this adapter.
For one response trait, gvc(variable = c(direct = "id", maternal = "dam"), traits = "BW", kernel = PED) declares an unstructured direct/maternal genetic covariance under one shared pedigree relationship. Covariance and prediction coordinates follow those channel names. Distinct descriptors remain independent; the adapter never infers correlation from matching IDs. Missing starts divide fixed-design residual variance over all channel diagonals and the residual, with zero off-diagonals. Observed responses require known IDs in all channels. See the direct/maternal example.
Residual gvc() descriptors now bind a variance-group column and optional AR(1) or exponential block/time columns to the existing component engine. AR(1) uses integer occasion gaps; exponential correlation uses actual numeric time distances. Every correlated block must belong to one variance group and contain unique positions. Named positive variance starts are matched to the observed group labels. Automatic starts use equal variance contributions, zero AR(1) correlation, or exponential correlation 0.2 at the median positive adjacent within-block time gap. No nugget, unknown-time imputation or automatic combination with random regression is introduced. See the residual workflow.
Detailed equations, layouts, ownership, and limitations remain in each repository’s local catalogue and linked design documents. The actual local dataset campaign is summarized separately in qgdata qualification.

title: Scientific model recipes
text:
These definitions preserve useful scientific distinctions from the earlier A-C planning catalog. They are mathematical recipes, not installed syntax, implementation priorities, or qualification claims. Consult the model catalog for each public route and the reductions for established equivalences.
For \(y = X\beta + \sum_k Z_k u_k + e\), each component must declare its external coefficient domain, record incidence and weights, relationship, covariance layout, missingness, and prediction targets. The notation Z describes the mathematics; it does not require a production incidence matrix.









Recipe
Scientific meaning and interpretation




Animal
\(a \sim \mathcal{N}(0,\sigma_a^2 A)\); records reference animal coefficients, including pedigree animals without observations


Multitrait animal
Relationship A shared across declared traits with covariance G; observed residual units use R[S,S]; different fixed designs and missing traits require explicit mapping


Repeatability
Independent animal and subject-level identity terms, plus residual; \(h^2 = v_a/(v_a+v_p+v_e)\) and repeatability \(\frac{v_a+v_p}{v_a+v_p+v_e}\)


Common environment
Independent identity component over litter, pen, household, herd, site, or another declared domain; domains need not be nested in pedigree order


Sire
Records reference sire coefficients with covariance \(\sigma_s^2 A_s\); report sire variance explicitly, without silently converting it to additive genetic variance


Direct/maternal
Animal and dam incidence channels share one pedigree relationship and a joint 2-by-2 genetic covariance; all dam references must resolve


Maternal permanent environment
Independent identity component indexed by dam; combining it with direct/maternal genetics gives the full maternal recipe


Trait-specific random effects
Components declare their acting traits and records; absent incidence is structural, distinct from a missing response


Correlated random coefficients
Several declared incidence channels share one relationship K and covariance Q; matching grouping labels alone do not imply correlation


Direct/social
Direct and social genetic channels may correlate, while a social channel has several weighted contributing group mates; self-exclusion, duplicates, weight scale, and member order need explicit contracts


Discrete pedigree GxE
Environment-specific breeding values with covariance \(A\otimes G_E\); a multitrait reduction applies only when incidence and fixed-design mappings match


Random regression/reaction norm
u_i has relationship-by-basis covariance and contributes \(b(t)^{\mathsf T}u_i\) or \(b(E)^{\mathsf T}u_i\); common-grid and irregular records use supplied bases, with explicit prediction rows and extrapolation interpretation



Repeatability and other variance ratios require a valid positive denominator and stated units; their uncertainty support must be assessed separately. For a trajectory, covariance between supplied basis rows is \(b(t)^{\mathsf T}Qb(s)\). Basis rank and external axis order are part of the model, not solver choices.



These families may apply to different domains. A family available in a generic longitudinal API is not thereby available in the component or formula API.







Family
Definition or required distinction




Homogeneous / heterogeneous diagonal
\(\sigma^2 I\) / \(\operatorname{diag}(\sigma_j^2)\); distinguish trait, residual-group, and level-domain variances


Unstructured SPD
\(LL^{\mathsf T}\) with positive diagonal L; log-Cholesky is a parameterization, not another covariance family


Compound symmetry
\(\sigma^2((1-\rho)I+\rho J)\); admissible rho depends on dimension


Heterogeneous compound symmetry
\(D((1-\rho)I+\rho J)D\), where D contains marginal standard deviations


Banded
Ordered levels and a declared bandwidth; specify omitted zeros and a positive-definite parameterization


Antedependence
Structured precision or modified Cholesky, with innovation variances and dependence coefficients; zero dependence reduces to diagonal covariance


Discrete AR(1)
\(\sigma^2\rho^{\lvert t_i-t_j\rvert}\) on integer positions, \(\lvert\rho\rvert<1\); heterogeneous scaling is \(DC_{\mathrm{AR1}}D\)


AR/MA/ARMA
Each order requires its own stationarity/invertibility, ordering, and derivative contract


Continuous exponential
\(\sigma^2\exp(-\phi\lvert t_i-t_j\rvert)\), \(\phi>0\), on irregular finite times; duplicate-time handling must be explicit


Unstructured within-subject residual
A bounded occasion covariance with observed principal submatrices; distinct from a permanent-environment random effect


Factor analytic FA(k)
\(\Lambda\Lambda^{\mathsf T}+\Psi\), positive diagonal specifics; declared rank and loading identification are required; compare derived covariances under permitted sign conventions


Reduced rank
\(\Lambda\Lambda^{\mathsf T}\) is singular when rank is below dimension; it requires an explicit singular precision/determinant/boundary contract


Spatial AR1 by AR1
\(\sigma^2 C_{\mathrm{row}}\otimes C_{\mathrm{col}}\); declare grid order and missing-cell behavior, separately from random row/column effects


General separable covariance
\(S_1\otimes S_2\); both factors need validated ordering and derivatives; \(\log\det(S_1\otimes S_2)=d_2\log\det(S_1)+d_1\log\det(S_2)\)



Support for one positive-interior family does not establish its zero-variance, singular, mixed-family, or optimized boundary extension. Component omission and fixed-parameter reductions remain useful when a chosen route excludes boundaries.

title: Multivariate sparse-pedigree evaluation and REML
text:
Multivariate sparse-pedigree evaluation and REML
gs_multitrait_pedigree_records() stores one row per observed scalar response. Rows sharing an observation-unit label belong to one animal and may contain any nonempty subset of the declared traits. A trait can occur once per unit; missing traits are absent and never imputed. Units are residual-independent, while traits observed together use the corresponding principal submatrix of the full SPD residual covariance R.
ped <- gs_pedigree_data(
  individual = c("child", "sire", "dam"),
  sire = c("sire", NA, NA), dam = c("dam", NA, NA))
records <- gs_multitrait_pedigree_records(
  ped,
  animal = c("sire", "sire", "dam", "child", "child"),
  trait = c("height", "weight", "height", "height", "weight"),
  observation_unit = c("sire", "sire", "dam", "child", "child"),
  phenotype = c(1.2, 2.0, .9, 1.8, 2.7),
  fixed = Matrix::Matrix(cbind(
    height_intercept = c(1, 0, 1, 1, 0),
    weight_intercept = c(0, 1, 0, 0, 1)), sparse = TRUE),
  trait_levels = c("height", "weight"))
start <- gs_multitrait_pedigree_start(records)
control <- gs_multitrait_pedigree_reml_control(
  linear_solver = "sparse_direct", direct_backend = "cholmod",
  exact_trace_method = "selected_inverse",
  maximum_selected_inverse_workspace_bytes = 2 * 1024^3,
  trace_mode = "complete_deterministic",
  maximum_direct_coefficient_dimension = 256,
  max_exact_trace_systems = 256, trace_batch_size = 32,
  requested_threads = 8)
fit <- gs_multitrait_pedigree_fit(
  records, start = start, covariance = "optimized", control = control)
The deterministic start fits the active fixed columns separately by trait and sets both starting covariance matrices to one half of the diagonal residual phenotypic variances. It does not estimate correlations and is not RHE. Explicit SPD G and R override it.
Three capability levels are intentional:

Large-scale fixed SPD G,R: sparse-PCG MME/BLUP, fixed effects, all-animal breeding values, record fitted/residual/Py, and stochastic fixed-parameter REML diagnostics.
Exact-work-limited sparse-direct estimation: one lower-CSC pattern and symbolic PARDISO or CHOLMOD analysis, deterministic coordinate traces in bounded retained-factor batches or one CHOLMOD supernodal selected-inverse derivative-support request per full trace evaluation, exact factor log determinants, and likelihood-monotone log-Cholesky optimization. Preflight reports coefficient dimension, input/factor nonzeros, trace systems, RHS workspace, fill, and factor memory, and enforces the configured limits.
Scalable stochastic estimation: PCG, fixed caller-controlled counter-Rademacher trace/determinant probes and seeds, common probes across accepted and trial states, standard batched AI, and noise-aware log-Cholesky optimization. Raw trace/score SEs are reported diagnostics; step admission and convergence use scale-aware curvature/Newton and standardized-score rules. An unresolved state returns insufficient_stochastic_precision without direct fallback.

The direct accepted state already contains the exact final likelihood. Rejected trials perform no trace or AI work, and final fixed effects and BLUPs reuse the accepted response coefficients without another factorization or solve. The result identifies fixed versus optimized covariance, trace mode, optimizer qualification, exact-work preflight, numerical and stochastic status, starting/final covariances, scores and AI, likelihood and SE, all-animal BLUPs, optional record values, retained-state reuse, observed patterns, sparse storage, PCG work, or direct symbolic/numerical factorization, solve, fill, memory, exact-trace, and thread-domain diagnostics.
Stochastic optimization returns separate optimizer, likelihood, and BLUP statuses. Score/AI convergence promotes the accepted covariance state and allows retained-response all-animal BLUP independently of final SLQ. If the requested log-determinant SE is not met, likelihood_available is false and the typed likelihood status is likelihood_precision_insufficient; the actual estimate, SE, probe/Lanczos configuration, and work remain diagnostic only. Likelihood-dependent model comparisons must require likelihood_available = TRUE. Exact sparse-direct REML is preferred for small or moderate problems within its resource limits, especially when an exact likelihood is required.
The qualified stochastic route retains standard batched AI. The separate augmented-AI experiment, component-LMM stochastic routes, and factor-analytic qualification boundaries are recorded in model qualification.
exact_trace_method = "coordinate" is the unchanged default and works with PARDISO or CHOLMOD. "selected_inverse" requires a resolved CHOLMOD backend and a sufficient maximum_selected_inverse_workspace_bytes limit. Derivative support is compiled once from a deterministic positive-definite planning state; one trace plan, derivative mapping, and selected-inverse workspace are reused across covariance states. It computes the exact inverse values on the coalesced covariance-derivative support, reports request/factor/workspace/peak-memory accounting, and performs zero coordinate trace systems. It does not remove the separately counted AI derivative-response systems. Explicit PARDISO, or automatic resolving to PARDISO, returns not_supported without fallback.
For direct fits, automatic prefers PARDISO. PARDISO retains qualified internal threading; CHOLMOD orchestration and multitrait support work remain 1/1 while selected-inverse dense kernels use their independently requested oneMKL thread count. PCG supports fixed-covariance solves and the stochastic REML route described above; both report zero direct work. An incompatible PARDISO selected-inverse request performs one symbolic capability resolution and then returns not_supported before numerical factorization.
The accepted factor, response, determinant, likelihood, and selected values are retained so BLUP finalization performs zero additional response solves. The shared typed serializer only translates native fields and performs no factorization, solve, trace, likelihood, score, AI, selected inversion, or BLUP work. In direct diagnostics, sparse_direct$requested is the logical direct-route flag; requested_backend and resolved_backend are backend strings.
The combined Windows process loads official Intel libiomp5md and no GNU libgomp; the CHOLMOD-only process loads no OpenMP runtime.
No route constructs dense pedigree, observation covariance, incidence, Kronecker, projection, or MME matrices. Exact covariance boundaries, PARDISO selected inversion, MUMPS, fixed-effect rank repair, general multiple relationship components, longitudinal direct REML through this API, RHE, marker effects, genomic or ssGBLUP models, and serial dependence between observation units are excluded.
Exact conditional PEV/reliability is specified separately in the prediction-error contract, including CHOLMOD selected inversion and bounded PARDISO retained-factor target solves.

title: Sparse-LD preparation contract
text:
gs_gprep(Glist, task = "sparseld", ...) validates an existing prepared gs_genotypes descriptor, resolves its physical BED rows and marker records, and delegates computation and persistence to gmat. gsuite owns only the public task, validation, selection, and returned R descriptor. gmat owns the numerical kernel, CSR storage, validation, and LD-score scan. gbits remains the existing packed BED access path. BED remains the genotype store, and neither a dense genotype matrix nor a dense genome-wide LD matrix is constructed.
The input is never prepared implicitly. Unknown tasks and the separate "ldscores" task fail. qgg and sblr are read-only qualification references and are not runtime dependencies.



Reference samples are selected by explicit ids, then Glist$study_ids, then all Glist$ids. Values must be nonempty, unique, nonmissing, and completely resolved. Caller order is preserved in idsLD, provenance, and the exact zero-based source rows passed to gmat.
Markers are selected by explicit rsids, otherwise all prepared markers. Requested IDs must be unique and completely resolved. The physical matrix is always ordered by file and original BIM order; requested order is recorded in provenance. source_marker_indices_0based supplies the original BED record for every marker, so noncontiguous preparation and LD subsets are safe. LD never crosses a chromosome boundary.
Allele frequencies count BIM field 5 (a1). Frequencies from preparation are reused only when the ordered LD samples equal the preparation sample set. Otherwise the existing gbits packed-count primitive recomputes frequencies for the LD reference rows; an all-missing marker fails. This frequency vector is aligned exactly to the CSR marker order. gmat independently obtains the same reference-sample means while standardizing genotypes.



For observed allele-1 dosage g, gmat uses \(p=\operatorname{mean}(g)/2\) and \(z=\frac{g-2p}{\sqrt{2p(1-p)}}\). A missing call is standardized zero, equivalent to mean imputation after centering. Monomorphic and all-missing columns have zero scale and become zero; gsuite rejects an all-missing selected reference marker before computation. Pairwise dot products accumulate in double precision and persisted correlations are signed float32 r. A zero denominator produces \(r=0\).
Only strict-upper off-diagonal entries satisfying \(r^2\geq\texttt{r2}\) are stored, in deterministic row/column order; the unit diagonal is implicit. A base-pair window and marker-index window are inclusive and combined with AND when both are positive. Zero disables one window. Both zero are rejected unless allow_full_ld = TRUE because that evaluates every same-chromosome pair.
Ordinary LD score is computed by scanning the validated persisted CSR: \(1+\sum r^2\) over retained off-diagonal neighbors. The implicit diagonal contributes one, thresholded-out entries do not contribute, and no finite- sample correction is applied. Scores follow rsidsLD exactly.



The canonical gmat format is sparse_ld_csr, format version 1. For prefix P, it owns exactly P.row_ptr.u64.bin, P.col_idx.u32.0based.bin, P.values.f32.bin, P.markers.tsv, and P.meta.txt. The first three contain a strict-upper CSR with zero-based columns and native fixed-width scalar types; the marker sidecar freezes identity and physical source mappings. Exact sizes, row pointers, sorted columns, finite values, dimensions, and marker metadata are validated before publication and on reopen.
Writes use a same-directory staging set. overwrite = FALSE refuses any existing owned target. Explicit overwrite replaces only that five-file set; metadata is published last as the commit marker. Staging and partially published new files are cleaned on failure.
The returned object remains c("gs_genotypes", "Glist"). Its canonical sparseLD member records prefix, format/version, paths, sample/marker counts, nnz, component files, physical one-based rows/cls, aligned AF, marker and sample IDs, zero-based mappings, thresholds/windows, block/thread settings, and provenance. Top-level ldfiles, rsidsLD, idsLD, and ldscores are deterministic compatibility views of that descriptor. No external pointer is stored, so saveRDS()/readRDS() is exact and the files can be reopened after reload.
The core payload layout is readable by the committed sblr CSR reader. the tested qgg 1.1.6 sparse-LD task instead writes fixed-width band files, so compatibility with qgg is numerical rather than a shared persistent format. No converter or sblr adapter is introduced.



Persistent input is the existing \(O(NM/4)\) BED and output is \(O(M + \mathrm{nnz})\). Working memory is bounded by \(O(M+\texttt{source\_N}+\texttt{selected\_N}\,\texttt{block\_size}+\texttt{active\_row\_nnz})\) plus per-row thread-local retained entries. It does not hold \(O(M^2)\) LD or \(O(NM)\) decoded genotypes. Realistic reference LD should be prepared once and reused.

title: AI-assisted research, methods, software and teaching
text:
What is AI?







Term
Meaning




Artificial intelligence
The broad field of building systems that perform tasks associated with human intelligence


Machine learning and deep learning
Methods that learn patterns from data. Deep learning uses neural networks with many layers


Generative AI
Models that generate text, code, images, audio or other content


AI assistants and agents
Systems built around generative AI that can work with users, files and tools. Agents can carry out multistep tasks



This presentation focuses on AI assistants and agents used for data analysis, method and software development, and teaching.

People use the term AI in different ways. Some think of machine learning or deep neural networks used to analyse data. Others think primarily of generative tools such as ChatGPT.
Machine learning covers methods that learn patterns from data. Deep learning is a form of machine learning based on neural networks with many layers. Modern generative AI is largely based on deep learning, but its purpose is to generate new content rather than only produce predictions.
Assistants interact with users and may have access to files and tools. Agents can use these capabilities to carry out more complex, multistep tasks.
This presentation concerns practical AI-assisted work. Applying machine learning as the scientific method being studied is outside its scope.

title: AI-assisted research, methods, software and teaching
text:
How researchers use generative AI







Activity
Examples




Writing and communication
Draft, revise, translate and shorten text


Literature work
Find relevant papers, summarise them and compare their conclusions


Data analysis
Inspect data, write code, make figures and explain results


Teaching
Develop slides, exercises, examples and explanations


Administration
Prepare emails, meeting notes, plans and reports



Writing and literature review are common entry points. The same technology can also contribute directly to mathematical, analytical and software work.

Many researchers first encounter generative AI as a writing assistant. It can also help identify literature, organise information, write analysis code and develop teaching material.
These uses still require review. Literature searches must be checked against the original sources, and scientific claims must not be accepted simply because the generated text sounds convincing.
My own use extends further into method and software development. That is the main focus of the following slides.

title: AI-assisted research, methods, software and teaching
text:
Areas of AI-assisted work








Area
Example output
Reusable result




Data analysis
An analysis script and report
A reproducible analysis workflow


Method development
A statistical model or algorithm
A clearly defined method with validation evidence


Software development
R and C++ code, interfaces and documentation
Tested and maintainable software components


Teaching
Slides, simulations and worked examples
Editable teaching materials



AI can help with mathematical reasoning, coding, analysis and documentation. Researchers set the scientific direction, review the decisions and determine what evidence is sufficient.

These activities are connected but distinct. A data-analysis question may reveal the need for a new statistical method. The method must then be translated into reliable software before it can be used routinely. A validated implementation can support new analyses and become a teaching example.
AI is particularly useful at the connection between mathematics and software. It can help examine equations, compare algorithms, implement them in R or C++, and prepare numerical checks. Researchers define the scientific problem, review the statistical and computational decisions, and decide what evidence is required.

title: AI-assisted research, methods, software and teaching
text:
Platforms developed with AI assistance







Platform
Purpose




gsuite
Statistical models, numerical computation and user interfaces


gsim
Simulation of genetic data and assessment of methods


gact
Data integration, annotation, analysis and interpretation


gteach
Shared tools and materials for teaching



AI has contributed to developing the platforms themselves. The resulting infrastructure can now support further work with AI assistants.

gtools


These platforms represent substantial outputs from AI-assisted development. The work has included mathematics, numerical algorithms, R and C++ code, interfaces, documentation, simulation, data organisation and teaching tools.
The platforms overlap and should not be assigned exclusively to individual uses. gsuite supports analysis, methods and software development. gsim supports method development and validation. gact supports data analysis and interpretation. qgteach connects research results with teaching.
The important point is cumulative. AI helped develop the infrastructure, and AI assistants can now use and extend what has already been built.

title: AI-assisted research, methods, software and teaching
section: From AI-assisted development to connected use
text:
From AI-assisted development to connected use


Building the platforms

Discuss mathematics and design with ChatGPT
Give Codex access to the relevant repositories
Implement methods, interfaces and documentation
Run checks, review changes and commit accepted work


Connecting the platforms now

Bring repositories and documentation into a shared workspace
Give the assistant access to existing capabilities
Use the platforms together for analysis and development
Extend them when a required capability is missing


The platforms came first. Connecting them to an AI assistant is the next step, and this work has only just begun.

From conversation to a reproducible analysis · From a scientific question to a supported model


I first used ChatGPT to discuss statistical models, mathematics, algorithms and software design. I then used Codex to work directly with the repositories, implement changes, compile the software, run checks and update documentation.
This process produced gsuite, gsim, gact and gteach as separate platforms.
I have only recently started bringing these platforms together in a shared ChatGPT workspace. The assistant can inspect the available repositories and documentation, use existing capabilities and identify where something is missing.
The two linked walkthroughs illustrate this newer phase. One shows how the assistant can help turn a question into a reproducible analysis. The other shows how a missing capability can lead to model and software development.
The longer-term opportunity is to make the platforms increasingly accessible to AI assistants while retaining scientific review and responsibility.

title: AI-assisted research, methods, software and teaching
text:
Using and extending the infrastructure


Use existing capabilities

Inspect the data and available tools
Specify the scientific model
Run and assess the analysis
Save the script and report


Add a missing capability

Identify the limitation
Define the required method or computation
Implement it using existing components
Validate and document the extension


Each completed project can improve the infrastructure available to the next.

AI assistants can work with the existing platforms rather than starting each project from scratch. They can inspect the available functionality, run analyses, modify code, add interfaces and prepare documentation.
Researchers remain responsible for defining the scientific problem, reviewing the statistical and computational decisions, and deciding whether the evidence is sufficient.

title: AI-assisted research, methods, software and teaching
text:
Data analysis infrastructure: gact
How can we make data from different sources usable in the same analysis?


Prepare and connect

Detect and validate data structures
Harmonise GWAS summary statistics
Add biological annotations
Record reusable ingestion steps


Analyse and interpret

Connect variants with genes and pathways
Use established statistical methods
Trace results back to their sources
Preserve the complete analysis workflow


The value comes from making data usable together.

gact


gact contains schema detection, normalisation and validation of GWAS summary statistics, ingestion recipes, biological annotation sets and database access. Existing tutorials connect these resources to gene analysis, fine-mapping and pathway analysis, including methods supplied by qgg.
This example concerns data preparation, connection and interpretation. It does not imply that every statistical method belongs within gact or that all four platforms already form one integrated pipeline.

title: AI-assisted research, methods, software and teaching
text:
Simulation for method development: gsim
How well does a method recover known quantities under different scenarios?


Define the scenario

Pedigree and population structure
Genetic architecture and effects
Phenotypes and environmental variation
Quantities that the method should recover


Assess the method

Compare estimates with known truth
Examine uncertainty and failures
Change the scenario and repeat
Identify where the method struggles


Simulation helps us develop, compare and refine methods under conditions where the truth is known.

gsim


gsim provides simulation infrastructure rather than owning every benchmark. It supports pedigrees, genotype and phenotype simulation, multiple genetic architectures and retained simulation truth. Study designs and evaluation metrics belong in the assessment workflow, for example sblrbench.
Our 10,000-animal pedigree examples use simulation to compare estimates and breeding values with known quantities. Replicated scenarios assess statistical behaviour. Independent small numerical references still provide a separate check of the implementation.

title: AI-assisted research, methods, software and teaching
text:
Software development: mathematics and code
AI is particularly useful when a project requires both mathematical reasoning and software implementation.


Mathematics

Interpret model equations
Derive computational expressions
Compare alternative algorithms
Identify assumptions and special cases


Software

Translate methods into R and C++
Inspect and modify existing code
Build interfaces and documentation
Run numerical comparisons and diagnostics


This supports a continuous process from a statistical idea to validated software.

gsuite


This has been one of the most important uses of AI in my work. The assistant can discuss the mathematics and then work directly with the implementation. For gsuite, this has included statistical models, numerical algorithms, C++ libraries, R interfaces, documentation and validation examples.
AI can make mistakes in both mathematics and code. I therefore define the statistical contract, review important decisions and require numerical evidence before treating a method as supported.

title: AI-assisted research, methods, software and teaching
section: Software from algorithms to interfaces: gsuite
text:
Software from algorithms to interfaces: gsuite







Layer
Examples




User interface
R functions such as gfit() and gvc()


Reusable model components
Covariance models, estimation and prediction


Native C++ and shared libraries
Solver interfaces, factor reuse and diagnostics


Numerical algorithms
Sparse solves and selected inverse entries



Development connects statistical ideas to efficient and usable software.

gsuite


Read the layers from bottom to top. Development includes numerical algorithms, native C++, shared libraries, reusable model components and the R interface. CHOLMOD and PARDISO are established external solvers that we build on. Our selected inverse uses retained CHOLMOD factors. The YAMS analogy concerns computing needed inverse entries, not a YAMS dependency.
greml owns model computations and gsolve owns solvers. The R interface exposes supported combinations. A Python interface remains a possible future addition and is therefore not presented here as a current capability.

title: AI-assisted research, methods, software and teaching
text:
The libraries behind gsuite








Repository
Main responsibility




gsuite
R interface: models, computational tasks and results


greml
Mixed models, REML estimation and prediction


gsolve
Numerical solvers, factor reuse and selected inverse calculations


gmat
Matrix operations, genotype panels and linkage disequilibrium


gbits
Compact genotype storage and operations on packed data


gcorr
Genetic correlation calculations


gscore
Genetic scoring and prediction


gbayes
Bayesian regression models




gsolve connects our model computations to established numerical libraries:
CHOLMOD / SuiteSparse and PARDISO → sparse matrix factorisation and linear solves.

This is a responsibility map, not a complete dependency graph. gsuite exposes selected capabilities through its R interface. gsim is a separate R package for simulation.
CHOLMOD and PARDISO are external libraries, not software developed by us. gsolve provides interfaces that allow supported model computations to use these sparse numerical backends. Other dense and iterative routes also exist.
Our selected-inverse implementation builds on retained CHOLMOD supernodal factors. It calculates required inverse entries without forming the full dense inverse. It does not use PARDISO for selected inversion.
AI-assisted development includes the algorithms and infrastructure around these external libraries, their integration, and the statistical and R layers.

AI-assisted gsuite development: numerical agreement and competitive runtime




Numerical agreement
50,000 animals
Maximum covariance-estimate difference below \(4.3\times10^{-8}\).
Prediction correlations above 0.999999999998 on the predeclared subset of 1,000 animals.

title: AI-assisted research, methods, software and teaching
text:
Where will AI lead us?


What is likely to change

Writing, coding and analysis will become faster
More groups will develop advanced methods and software
AI assistants will perform increasingly complex tasks
Research roles and expectations will change


Questions for our programme

Which expertise and resources will distinguish us?
How should we combine AI with our data and infrastructure?
Which capabilities should we develop and share?
How should training, review and responsibility change?


What should we change now to remain scientifically distinctive as AI becomes part of research?

AI is already part of research, and its capabilities will continue to develop. Routine use of writing assistants or code generation will become common. The strategic question concerns how this changes our research and what will remain distinctive.
Scientific questions, domain knowledge, trusted data, critical evaluation and responsibility will remain important. Our shared platforms provide one possible advantage because they capture expertise in infrastructure that researchers and AI assistants can use and extend.
We should discuss which capabilities we need, how our roles may change, and where we should invest to remain scientifically strong.

section: From a computational need to a component
text:
From a computational need to a component
Need: Obtain required inverse entries without forming a full dense inverse.







Step
What we work through with AI




Build small references
Dense inverse and scalar Takahashi calculations in C++


Implement the efficient algorithm
Selected inversion using retained CHOLMOD factors


Compare in native tests
Check requested entries against both references


Check computational behaviour
Factor reuse, thread agreement and retained solves


Integrate and assess
Supported model computations and the R workflow



Reference and production calculations are both native C++.

The development pattern is to establish a small reference, implement the efficient algorithm, compare them, and then check broader computational and user workflows. This describes the documented validation structure rather than asserting the exact historical order of every implementation step. gsolve/docs/testing.md and tests/test_supernodal_selected_inverse.cpp document and implement two small C++ references: a dense inverse and a separate scalar Takahashi recurrence. Requested entries from the production supernodal route are compared with both. The scalar reference is test-only, not an installed production fallback. Additional assertions check repeated factorisation, thread agreement, and preservation of retained solves and log-determinants. CHOLMOD is external; our production route uses its retained supernodal factors without forming the full dense inverse. PARDISO is not used for this selected inversion. These are test contracts, not a claim that every current test passes.

title: AI-assisted research, methods, software and teaching
text:
Different checks answer different questions







Check
Question it addresses




Mathematics and special cases
Does the formulation represent the intended model?


Small native reference versus production algorithm
Do separate computational approaches agree?


Repeated simulation with known truth
How well does the method recover quantities across scenarios?


Comparison with other software
Do results agree for matched models and settings?


Complete user workflow
Can the interface produce an interpretable, reproducible result?



Independence comes from a separate computational approach, not a different programming language.

These checks complement one another. Both reference and production code can be C++. greml retains small dense, analytical and finite-difference checks in native tests; gmat uses explicit dense correlation and LD calculations; gbits compares optimised implementations with scalar references. Their testing.md guides describe the assertions and reference limitations. Not every comparison has the same degree of independence: two wrappers over the same engine do not provide an independent numerical reference. Agreement between programs requires matching models, conventions and settings. Simulation can assess bias, uncertainty and prediction, but the generating model and studied scenarios limit what we learn. Runtime comparisons require explicit work boundaries. Define tolerances and acceptance criteria before interpreting results, and record the model, route and scale covered by the evidence.

title: AI-assisted research, methods, software and teaching
text:
Where human judgement enters


Scientific decisions

Which question matters?
Which assumptions fit the study?
Which quantities should we estimate?
What can the results support?


Development decisions

Which approximations are acceptable?
What should be implemented or reused?
Which checks are sufficient?
When is a result ready to share?


AI can help examine each decision. We remain responsible for accepting it.

Human judgement is present throughout the process, not only in a final review. The researcher contributes study knowledge and statistical reasoning; software developers contribute computational and engineering judgement. AI can propose alternatives, expose assumptions, implement choices and assemble checks. Important decisions should remain visible in model definitions, code review, documentation and the interpretation of the evidence.

title: AI-assisted research, methods, software and teaching
text:
What remains after the conversation?


A reusable analysis or method

Model definition and assumptions
Code and an executable example
Tests and numerical evidence


Enough information to revisit it

Data identity, settings and versions
Results and documented limitations
Explanations and teaching material


The next researcher should be able to understand and use the work without reading the chat.

Conversation helps us develop the work, but it is not a substitute for its reproducible outputs. Keep the relevant data provenance, source revisions, settings and random seeds alongside results. Documentation should describe the final implementation and its limitations. Store reviewed evidence rather than every temporary experiment. This is what lets progress in one project benefit another, with or without the same assistant.
